register.name: New 38-month Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Staff-level agreement 8 October 2026, with the 2026 Article IV consultation · SDR 150.02 million, 114% of quota · Board meeting expected in early December 2026
register.note: About US$203 million; SDR 26.3244 million (about US$36 million) on completion of the tenth review and approval of the request
register.text: A new three-year programme agreed by IMF staff in Niamey on 8 October 2026, to follow the current Extended Credit Facility. Staff expect growth of 7% in 2026 and 6.7% in 2027, with the fiscal deficit projected at 3.4% of GDP in 2026; it supports the public finances behind the seven standards.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved December 2021 · extended twelve months to December 2026 · access augmented by 60% of quota · ninth review completed 29 July 2026 · tenth and final review agreed by staff 8 October 2026
register.note: SDR 228.06 million (about US$306 million) disbursed by March 2026; SDR 24.0828 million (about US$33 million) agreed for the ninth review
register.text: The IMF’s main lending programme with Niger since 2021, supporting oil revenue management and public financial management reforms. Its tenth and final review was agreed by staff on 8 October 2026, with Board consideration expected in early December 2026.

register.name: Electricity access, including the Kandadji Dam programme
register.detail: World Bank · One national and four regional projects, including Haské and the Kandadji Dam programme
register.note: More than one million people gained access to electricity through Haské between January and October 2026
register.text: The World Bank mobilises $1.2 billion for one national and four regional energy projects, including the Kandadji Dam programme, to bring electricity to more than 4.5 million people. Haské, the Niger Accelerating Electricity Access Project, combines grid expansion with solar mini-grids, off-grid solar and clean cooking; it serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 5 July 2023 · 75% of quota · extended to 4 March 2026 · fourth review completed 13 March 2026
register.note: About US$131.5 million; SDR 98.702 million disbursed in all by March 2026
register.text: The IMF’s climate resilience arrangement with Niger, run alongside the Extended Credit Facility. Its fourth review, in March 2026, released SDR 21.714 million (about US$30 million) and brought disbursements to the full amount of the arrangement.

register.name: Support to the Financial Sector and Access to MSME Finance in Niger Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Grant approved 12 March 2026 · liquidity support, risk-sharing and technical assistance · contingent emergency response component
register.note: About 7,500 micro, small and medium enterprises to be reached and an estimated 58,000 jobs created or maintained
register.text: An IDA grant that addresses cash shortages at banks and microfinance institutions and weak public sector banks, to restore lending to viable small businesses, with targeted support to women-led businesses. It serves livelihood.

register.name: Improving Women’s and Girls’ Access to Improved Health and Nutrition Services in the Priority Areas Project (LAFIA-IYALI)
register.note: Listed on World Bank Finances One; the type of financing is not stated there
register.text: Finances better access for women and girls to health and nutrition services in priority areas of Niger. It serves health and food.

register.name: Niger Food Security and Emergency Access to Essential Services Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 5 June 2025 · two financings, $131.1 million and $88.9 million
register.note: Sum of the two financings listed on World Bank Finances One
register.text: A World Bank operation for food security and emergency access to essential services, approved in two parts on 5 June 2025. It serves food, the standard on which 50.3% of Nigeriens are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Southern Niger Connectivity and Integration Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Release of 19 May 2025 · $380 million credit and $20 million grant · Maradi–Zinder section of National Road 1 · 525 km of feeder and rural roads
register.note: National Road 1 and its feeder network serve over 16 million people in Niger and Nigeria
register.text: Rehabilitates the Maradi–Zinder section of National Road 1 and makes 525 km of feeder and rural roads climate-resilient, with reforms to road maintenance. All-season roads bring markets, health centres, schools and jobs within reach; it serves livelihood, health and education.

register.name: Project for the Improvement of Connectivity in North-East Niger (PACNEN), additional financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Release of 7 April 2025 · National Road 11, the Trans-Saharan Corridor, Zinder–Agadez · maintenance through 2031 · 200 km of rural roads
register.note: More than 170,000 people living near the corridor expected to benefit directly
register.text: Additional IDA financing to rehabilitate National Road 11 between Zinder and Agadez, maintain the corridor through 2031 and upgrade 200 km of rural roads to climate-resilient standards. It serves livelihood, for the traders, farmers and transporters along the route.

register.name: Strengthening the operational capacity of the National Office for Hydro-Agricultural Development (ONAHA)
register.detail: BOAD · Approved at the 151st ordinary session of the Board, Lomé, 26 June 2026
register.note: One of two BOAD operations for Niger approved on 26 June 2026
register.text: Strengthens the National Office for Hydro-Agricultural Development, to increase developed land areas and agricultural production. It serves food.

register.name: Electricity Generation Capacity Strengthening Project (PRECAP2E)
register.detail: BOAD · Approved at the 151st ordinary session of the Board, Lomé, 26 June 2026 · diesel plants and solar photovoltaic mini-plants
register.text: Deploys diesel power plants and solar photovoltaic mini-plants to strengthen the nation’s power generation capacity. It serves energy, where 21.3% of Nigeriens have electricity.

register.name: Niger–Benin pipeline tariff agreement
register.note: Read in the Coface country risk file; no CNPC or government release found yet
register.text: An agreement with CNPC cutting the transport rate on the Niger–Benin pipeline to the Benin terminal from $27 to $15 a barrel. A cheaper route to the sea leaves more of the value of each barrel in Niger.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil Line
items.label: Pipeline tariff a barrel to the Atlantic, 2026
items.text: A landlocked nation now selling oil by sea; the cheaper the barrel travels, the more stays at home.

items.name: The Power to Come
items.label: People who gained electricity through Haské, January to October 2026
items.text: A nation where one in five has power is connecting the rest, with the Kandadji Dam at its heart.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Farms and herds that carry most families, from the river to the Sahel.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Territory to farm, mine, power and protect.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 46.2% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Fasam Terre Verte
items.text: A cooperative founded in 2021 that produces and distributes organic inputs for farmers: seeds, natural fertilisers and biological crop protection suited to Sahelian conditions. In March 2026 I&P Accélération lent it 40,000,000 CFA francs, paid in three instalments tied to performance targets.

items.name: OUBA Energy and Technology
items.text: Sells solar kits to off-grid rural households in Niger on pay-as-you-go terms, combining last-mile logistics, digital payment tracking and trained local agents. Its D-Prize pilot aims to reach 500 households, about 3,500 people, in three to five unelectrified communities.

items.name: Mayaki Trading
items.text: Sells solar kits, batteries, mini power plants and inverters, with about 75% of its revenue from clean energy. Support from I&P Accélération from July 2025 covered a container of about 3,000 solar kits, for users who cannot rely on the public grid.

items.name: Hi-Tech Solutions
items.text: Founded in 2013, it distributes solar panels, inverters and photovoltaic components to rural and peri-urban communities in Niger, and has been in the I&P Accélération au Sahel portfolio since 2022.

items.name: Likita Care
items.text: Designs and builds in Niger a connected monitoring platform for hospitals and clinics, tracking patients, cardiac function and prenatal health from one dashboard. More than 70 units are in use across five medical centres; it won the 2026 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation.
